Plot the ranks of features over time

Source: R/AllGenerics.R, R/plotRanks.R, R/zzz-mae.R
plotRanks.Rd

plotRanks() draws the abundance rank of the most abundant features in each sample as bump lines, one panel per subject. In polar coordinates the plot becomes a rank clock.

Usage

plotRanks(x, ...)

# S4 method for class 'SummarizedExperiment'
plotRanks(
  x,
  time.col,
  group = NULL,
  assay.type = "counts",
  features = NULL,
  top = 5,
  coord = c("cartesian", "polar"),
  max.gap = NULL,
  ...
)

# S4 method for class 'MultiAssayExperiment'
plotRanks(x, ..., experiment = 1L)

Arguments

x

a SummarizedExperiment object.

...

additional arguments passed to geom_line.

time.col

Character scalar. Specifies the column from colData(x) that contains sampling times: numeric, Date, POSIXct or a factor of visits. Time differences, as in max.gap, are in days for Date and hours for POSIXct times.

group

Character scalar. Specifies the column from colData(x) that identifies subjects. If NULL, all samples form one series. (Default: NULL)

assay.type

Character scalar. Specifies the assay of abundances. To rank taxa such as phyla, agglomerate x first with mia::agglomerateByRank(). (Default: "counts")

features

Character vector. Features to draw. If NULL, draws the top features with the best mean rank. (Default: NULL)

top

Integer scalar. Number of features to draw when features is NULL. (Default: 5)

coord

Character scalar. Draws time on a straight ("cartesian") or circular ("polar") axis. (Default: "cartesian")

max.gap

Numeric scalar. Breaks a line where consecutive samples of a subject are further apart than this, in time.col units. For visits, NULL breaks lines at visits without a sample; otherwise NULL never breaks lines. (Default: NULL)

experiment

Character scalar or integer scalar. For a MultiAssayExperiment, the experiment to plot; its samples get the colData of x. (Default: 1L)

Value

A ggplot object.

Details

Ranks are among all features of a sample, 1 the most abundant; ties get their mean rank.

References

Collins SL, et al. (2008). Rank clocks and plant community dynamics. Ecology 89(12):3534-3541.

Examples

# 16 species in three bioreactors
data("minimalgut", package = "miaTime")
tse <- minimalgut
plotRanks(tse, time.col = "Time.hr", group = "StudyIdentifier")


# As rank clocks
plotRanks(tse, time.col = "Time.hr", group = "StudyIdentifier",
    coord = "polar")


# Phyla of the subjects sampled five times
data("hitchip1006", package = "miaTime")
tse <- hitchip1006[, !duplicated(t(SummarizedExperiment::assay(
    hitchip1006, "counts")))]
tse <- tse[, tse$subject %in% names(which(table(tse$subject) == 5))]
tse <- mia::agglomerateByRank(tse, rank = "Phylum")
plotRanks(tse, time.col = "time", group = "subject", top = 3)
